breakfast.name: Pupusas
instructions: Mix masa dough
Fill with cheese/beans/chicharrón
Shape into thick tortillas
Cook on griddle until golden spots appear
Serve with curtido and salsa
breakfast.description: El Salvador's national dish — thick stuffed corn tortillas.

breakfast.name: Platanos Fritos con Crema
instructions: Slice plantains lengthwise
Fry until golden and caramelized
Serve with crema and beans
breakfast.description: Fried sweet plantains with cream and beans.

breakfast.name: Pupusa Revuelta (Mixed Filling Pupusa)
ingredients: Filling: chicharrón (ground pork cracklings), refried beans, quesillo cheese
Curtido: cabbage, carrot, red onion, oregano, vinegar
instructions: Mix masa harina with water and salt — dough should be smooth and pliable, not sticky
Take a ball of dough, press flat in your palm
Add a spoonful of mixed filling — beans, chicharrón, and cheese together
Close the dough around the filling, pat back into a flat disc — the filling is sealed inside
Cook on a hot, dry griddle — no oil needed — until brown spots form on both sides
The cheese should melt and start oozing at the edges — this is the sign of a perfect pupusa
Serve with curtido (vinegar slaw) and thin tomato salsa
Pupusa revuelta is the most popular filling — the holy trinity of bean, pork, cheese
This is El Salvador's NATIONAL dish — declared national cultural heritage, pupusa day is the 2nd Sunday in November
breakfast.description: El Salvador's national treasure — a thick corn cake with a mixed filling of beans, pork cracklings, and cheese, griddled until the cheese oozes. The hand-patting technique and the cheese-ooze moment are the most viral Salvadoran food videos. Pupusas have an official national holiday (2nd Sunday of November) — no other dish in Central America has that honor.

lunch.name: Sopa de Pata (Cow Foot Soup)
instructions: Boil cow foot and tripe 90 min
Add vegetables, cook 30 min
Add cilantro
Squeeze lime to serve
lunch.description: Rich, hearty cow foot soup — Salvadoran weekend tradition.

lunch.name: Casamiento (Married Rice and Beans)
instructions: Sauté onion, garlic, pepper
Add beans, rice, and water
Cook covered until rice is tender
Season with Worcestershire
lunch.description: Rice and beans cooked together — 'the marriage'.

lunch.name: Sopa de Pata (Cow Foot Soup)
ingredients: Yuca, green plantain, corn on the cob (cut into rounds)
instructions: Boil cow foot pieces for 2-3 hours until tender and the broth is gelatinous
Add tripe, cook another 30 min
Add yuca, plantain, corn — cook until tender
Add cabbage and chayote in last 15 min
Season broth with tomatoes, onion, garlic, achiote, cumin, oregano
The broth should be rich and slightly gelatinous from the cow foot collagen
Serve in deep bowls with lime and hot sauce
This is El Salvador's weekend and hangover soup — the collagen broth is the cure
lunch.description: El Salvador's legendary cow foot soup — hours of simmering render the collagen into a rich, gelatinous broth loaded with root vegetables and corn. The ultimate Salvadoran weekend and hangover cure. The gelatinous broth texture and the nose-to-tail tradition have made sopa de pata viral in the 'overlooked soups' genre.

dinner.name: Pollo Guisado (Salvadoran Braised Chicken)
instructions: Season chicken with cumin, oregano, achiote
Brown in oil
Add tomatoes, onion, pepper, garlic
Add potatoes and water
Braise 30 min
Serve with rice and tortillas
dinner.description: Braised chicken in tomato sauce with potatoes.

dinner.name: Yuca Frita con Chicharrón
instructions: Boil yuca until tender
Deep fry until golden and crispy
Serve with chicharrón, curtido, and tomato sauce
dinner.description: Crispy fried yuca with pork cracklings.

dinner.name: Tamales de Elote (Sweet Corn Tamales)
ingredients: 12 ears fresh sweet corn (grated or blended)
instructions: Grate fresh corn kernels or blend briefly — keep texture
Mix corn pulp with sugar, melted butter, salt
Spoon mixture onto corn husks, fold and tie
Steam for 40-45 min until firm
Unwrap — the tamale should be sweet, moist, and hold its shape
Serve with crema on top
These are dessert tamales — sweet, not savory — and made only when corn is in season
The fresh corn flavor is irreplaceable — canned or frozen won't work
dinner.description: Sweet tamales made from fresh corn — not masa, but actual grated corn ears — steamed in husks. Seasonal and irreplaceable (you can't fake fresh corn). The sweet corn aroma when unwrapping and the crema drizzle are viral Salvadoran food moments.

snacks.name: Pastelitos de Carne
ingredients: Filling: ground beef, potatoes, tomato, onion
instructions: Make masa dough
Cook filling: beef, potato, tomato, onion
Fill dough, fold, seal edges
Deep fry until golden

snacks.name: Yuca Frita con Chicharrón (Fried Yuca with Pork)
instructions: Boil yuca until tender but not mushy
Cut into wedges
Deep fry until golden and crispy outside, fluffy inside
Serve piled with chicharrón on top
Accompany with curtido and tomato salsa
The yuca should be crunchier than french fries on the outside, creamier inside
This is El Salvador's answer to fries — and once you try it, potatoes feel boring
snacks.description: El Salvador's answer to french fries — fried cassava wedges that are crunchier outside and creamier inside than any potato. Topped with crispy pork and tangy slaw. The 'better than fries' comparison has made yuca frita viral as people discover it's a cassava world and potatoes are just living in it.

desserts.name: Semita Pacha
instructions: Make sweet dough with panela
Roll out, spread guava paste
Top with more dough
Bake at 175°C 45 min
Cut into squares
desserts.description: Layered cake with guava paste and panela.

desserts.name: Semita Pacha (Salvadoran Sweet Bread)
ingredients: Dough: flour, sugar, butter, eggs, yeast, anise, vanilla
instructions: Make sweet yeast dough with anise and vanilla — let rise 1 hour
Roll out, spread with thick panela syrup
Fold, roll again, spread more syrup — building layers
Shape into rounds
Let rise 30 min
Brush with egg wash
Bake at 180°C for 20-25 min until golden
The panela layers inside create dark, sweet stripes when sliced
This is El Salvador's traditional sweet bread — found in every bakery
desserts.description: El Salvador's traditional layered sweet bread — the panela syrup between layers creates dark sweet stripes when sliced. Flavored with anise, it's found in every Salvadoran bakery. The cross-section with its striped layers has gained attention in the global artisan bread scene.

drinks.name: Horchata Salvadoreña
instructions: Toast and grind morro seeds, sesame, rice
Boil with cocoa, cinnamon, vanilla
Strain, add sugar
Serve cold over ice
drinks.description: Salvadoran horchata — nuttier and spicier than the Mexican version.

drinks.name: Atol de Elote (Corn Drink)
instructions: Cut corn from cobs
Blend with milk
Cook with sugar and cinnamon until thick
Serve warm
